differential: Pulmonary embolism
Sudden onset dyspnea in a middle-aged woman is a classic presentation for PE, especially given age-related risk factors.
Acute myocardial infarction
Sudden dyspnea can be an anginal equivalent in women, who often present atypically without chest pain.
Acute exacerbation of asthma
Sudden breathlessness could represent bronchospasm, though no prior history is mentioned yet.
Pneumothorax
Spontaneous pneumothorax can present with sudden dyspnea, though more common in certain body habitus or underlying lung disease.
Acute heart failure
Sudden decompensation of cardiac function can present with acute dyspnea in this age group.

differential: Pulmonary embolism
Recent femur fracture with prolonged immobilization during rehab creates high risk for venous thromboembolism causing fatal PE.
Fat embolism syndrome
Femur fracture 3 months prior can cause delayed fat embolism leading to sudden respiratory compromise and cardiac arrest.
Acute myocardial infarction
Sudden cardiac arrest in a 58-year-old woman could result from acute coronary syndrome with fatal arrhythmia.
Aortic dissection
Sudden onset dyspnea followed by rapid cardiovascular collapse is consistent with acute type A dissection.
Massive hemorrhage
Post-rehabilitation complications such as occult bleeding or delayed trauma sequelae could cause hypovolemic shock and arrest.
eliminated: Pneumothorax
While causing dyspnea, tension pneumothorax with failed resuscitation is less likely without trauma or procedural history at presentation.
Asthma exacerbation
Fatal asthma would typically have prodromal symptoms and respond to initial resuscitation efforts in most cases.

differential: Fat embolism
Recent femur fracture with fibrous organization of embolic material in pulmonary vessels causing sudden fatal cardiopulmonary collapse.
Pulmonary thromboembolism with organization
Deep vein thrombosis from immobilization post-fracture with organized thrombus showing fibrous remodeling in pulmonary arteries.
Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Organized fibrous tissue from recurrent emboli causing pulmonary vascular remodeling and acute decompensation.
Tumor embolism
Occult malignancy with tumor emboli to pulmonary vasculature eliciting fibrous reaction and acute cardiovascular collapse.
Amniotic fluid embolism
Though age makes pregnancy unlikely, fibrin and cellular debris can cause pulmonary vascular fibrosis and sudden death.
eliminated: Acute myocardial infarction
Autopsy findings focus on pulmonary vascular pathology rather than coronary or myocardial changes.
Primary pulmonary artery sarcoma
Would show malignant tissue rather than organized fibrous connective tissue around vessel lumen.
Pneumonia
Would show inflammatory infiltrates in alveoli rather than fibrous tissue specifically around pulmonary artery lumens.

differential: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH)
Organized thrombi with recanalization and fibrous tissue around pulmonary arteries are pathognomonic findings, with history of femur fracture as initial embolic source.
Acute-on-chronic pulmonary embolism
Recent acute embolic event superimposed on chronic thromboembolic disease from prior femur fracture explains sudden decompensation and death.
Pulmonary artery sarcoma
Can mimic chronic thromboembolism histologically and cause pulmonary artery occlusion, though organized thrombi with recanalization make this less likely.
Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease
Can cause fibrous changes in pulmonary vasculature, though typically affects veins rather than arteries and lacks organized thrombi.
Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension with in-situ thrombosis
Could cause pulmonary artery remodeling with secondary thrombosis, though chronic organized thrombi point more toward embolic origin.
eliminated: Primary vasculitis (e.g., Takayasu arteritis)
Autopsy shows organized thrombi rather than inflammatory vessel wall changes typical of vasculitis.
Fat embolism syndrome
Would present acutely after fracture (3 months ago) and does not cause chronic organized thrombi with recanalization.
Amniotic fluid embolism
Patient demographics and chronic histological findings incompatible with this acute peripartum condition.
